newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean riot officer dies in student violence.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean riot officer dies in student violence.

text.p: A South Korean riot policeman died of injuries after being beaten by students armed with metal bars during fierce clashes on Monday outside a Seoul university, a police official said.
The 21-year-old officer, Yoo Ji-woong, died in hospital, the official said but gave no more details.
It was the first fatality in four straight days of violent protests by as many as 10,000 students demanding the resignation of President Kim Young-sam.
Witnesses said a number of police officers were beaten senseless by left-wing students outside Hanyang University. Some had their clothes set on fire by petrol bombs hurled by the rioters.
Injured officers were sprawled helplessly on the streets, their helmets scattered around them, witnesses said.

Hand-to-hand fighting erupted as students burst through ranks of police blocking a bridge leading to the college, where an outlawed left-wing student body was planning an inauguration ceremony for new office holders.
Students seized about 10 officers and were holding them outside the college gates.
One group attacked an armoured police teargas launcher with metal pipes, smashing its windows and sides. Many young rioters sported white headbands saying "Kim Young-sam Resign".
A young riot officer with a badly injured leg begged for help from students. Several police officers tried to escape the fighting by dashing inside the campus.
Prosecutors on Monday vowed to "deal sternly" with the violence, orchestrated by the outlawed Hanchongryon body, which the government maintains is a stooge of rival North Korea.

"We will deal sternly with any student violence. This violence is unacceptable. We will seek out any pro-communist students and punish them severely," said Shin Gun-soo, a senior prosecutor at the Seoul Prosecution Office.
The violence was sparked by Kim's refusal to bow to opposition demands and reveal how much he spent on his 1992 election campaign.
Allegations that Kim grossly overspent have surfaced in the final year of his presidency in the wake of a corruption scandal involving loans to bankrupt Hanbo Steel.
The scandal has led to the arrest of one of Kim's sons and several of his closest aides, shattering his credibility.
